solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Highlander born outside areas of settlement

indicators.note: the word for born goes around, outside, the areas of settlement

parts.note: née, from French, means born, used before a maiden name
a pale was a fenced district of settlement, as in the English Pale in Ireland

explanation.surface: A mountain dweller was born somewhere beyond the settled districts.
explanation.walkthrough: Highlander here is not a Scot but someone from the Himalayan kingdom; 'the Pale' was the settled English enclave in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Nepal lives among the Himalayas, so is literally a mountain dweller.

clue.text: Exercise cancelled? On the contrary

parts.note: something cancelled is a no-go, so cancelled gives NO
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the workout has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' does double duty in spirit: the pieces come in the opposite order to the clue, and the answer is a flat contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A slangy flat denial contradicts what was just said, much like 'on the contrary'.

clue.text: Who makes one fit one's own footwear?

parts.note: something personal belongs to one alone
a trainer is a sports shoe (a sneaker)

explanation.surface: A riddle about who might fit a shoe on someone's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like fitting shoes, but means physically fit; 'trainer' is the British word for a sneaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym coach engaged by an individual works to get that client into good physical shape.

clue.text: In protective coat, regularly beat beast up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the combined letters are read from bottom to top
taking every other letter of beat leaves its second and fourth letters

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: Someone in armour beats a beast, upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ET from bEaT; ETANIMAL read 'up' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To laminate something is to seal it in a thin protective layer of plastic, i.e. put it in a protective coat.

clue.text: Dumb, forms words silently in turn, picking Oscar out

indicators.note: turned round, so the remaining letters are read backwards
picking a letter out of a word means removing it, here with out
completes picking ... out, removing the letter

parts.note: to mouth words is to form them with the lips without sound
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A mute person mouths words in sequence, avoiding the letter O.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking Oscar out' takes O from MOUTHS, leaving MUTHS; 'in turn' reverses it. The answer is Yiddish-derived British slang for keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping schtum means staying silent, so the slang word is a synonym of mute.

clue.text: Fail to penetrate record that's restricted

indicators.note: the word for fail goes into the record's letters

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a record
to lose is to fail, as in a contest

explanation.surface: A failed attempt to break into a classified file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail' is the verb lose, and 'record' a compact disc; 'to penetrate' sends the first into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed meeting or event is restricted to certain people only.

clue.text: Extremely fashionable city, international

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A chic cosmopolitan city is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest styles are the most in vogue, a superlative of being up to date.

clue.text: Autobiography the Brontės ordered?

parts.note: to be summoned is to be ordered to come
the Brontë sisters first published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell, so their books were by Bells

explanation.surface: An autobiography in which the Brontë sisters gave orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is vague; the hint is the Brontës' pen-name surname Bell. The answer is John Betjeman's verse autobiography.
explanation.definitionFit: John Betjeman's blank-verse account of his own early life bears this title, so it is a memoir.

clue.text: Deprive of spirits, but find way to make better beer?

definitions.text: find way to make better beer?
definitions.meaning: removing the middle TT from better leaves beer

explanation.surface: A teetotal improver both removes the spirits and seeks a better beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests alcohol but means morale. The second reading splits the answer as un-heart: remove the heart (TT) of 'better' and you have 'beer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to sap their morale, leaving them low in spirits.

clue.text: Without feeling stiff, race round

indicators.note: the word for race goes round the word for stiff

parts.note: to fly is to race, rush along
rigid means stiff

explanation.surface: Someone stiff and numb races around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without feeling' looks like part of the surface's numbness but is the whole definition; 'round' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting coldly means acting with no warmth or emotion, i.e. without feeling.

clue.text: Right time, curiously, to punch Lord's boundary

indicators.note: the shuffled letters punch into, go inside, the word for lord

parts.note: a lord is a peer; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: the letters of time are arranged in a curious new order

explanation.surface: A batsman times a shot perfectly to hit the boundary at Lord's cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' makes IMET of time; 'to punch' puts R and that inside the lord. Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, but here it is just a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer edge enclosing an area is its boundary line or circumference.

clue.text: Losing height, river gets less fierce

indicators.note: the river's name loses a letter

parts.note: the Thames is London's river

explanation.surface: A river in drought falls and becomes calmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' drops H from THAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To tame is to make or become gentle and docile, less wild.

clue.text: Wow! New for old material

definitions.note: trite, stale stuff, as in a corny joke

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A cry of delight at swapping old fabric for new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation like 'gosh'. 'New for old' suggests a swap, but the pieces are simply COR and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed, sentimental jokes and routines are known as corny stuff: tired old material.

clue.text: It could turn into some great outlet

indicators.note: the letters of some great could be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A small shop might grow into a great retail outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could turn into' signals rearranging SOME GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant retail shop is an outlet, a place where goods are sold.

clue.text: Averting maiden, miscue balls horribly: declaration follows this?

indicators.note: the letters of miscue balls, with the maiden averted, are horribly jumbled

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden (over)

explanation.surface: A cricketer avoids a maiden over by miscuing balls badly before declaring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Averting maiden' removes M from MISCUE BALLS; 'horribly' jumbles the rest. Cricket terms (maiden over, declaration) mislead; the declaration is of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase for an act justifying war, which a declaration of war would follow.

clue.text: A vehicle finally left US yard, almost boldly innovative

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: only the last letter of left is used
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Americans call a garden a yard; garden is the British word

explanation.surface: A van drives away from an American yard, nearly empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T from 'left'; 'almost' trims GARDEN to GARDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneering work that pushes artistic boundaries ahead of the mainstream is boldly innovative.

clue.text: All agreed a descendant has rejected title

parts.note: a son is a descendant

indicators.note: turned back, so the title's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: An heir has turned down a hereditary title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses NAME to EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison, everyone together with one accord, is an idiom for unanimous agreement.

clue.text: Our team's shortened clothing

indicators.note: the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: our team is we, and team's is team is, so we are

explanation.surface: Our team's kit has been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our team's' = WE ARE; 'shortened' drops the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments of a given kind, as in sportswear or menswear, are collectively called this.

clue.text: It's unclear Thomas was like this

definitions.meaning: the apostle Thomas refused to believe in the Resurrection without proof, hence a doubting Thomas

explanation.definitionFit: Something uncertain is questionable, and the sceptical apostle was full of uncertainty.

clue.text: As far as university, carry on reading

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to continue on the next page

explanation.surface: A student keeps reading all the way to university.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO is written at the foot of a page: please turn over.
explanation.definitionFit: Going until a point means reaching as far as it.

clue.text: Stuntman died — son swallowing this stiff drink

indicators.note: the word for son takes in the letter for died

parts.note: a son is a boy
a double is a large measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A stuntman has died, and his son knocks back a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts D inside BOY. 'Stiff' tempts as corpse, but it qualifies the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in who takes an actor's place for dangerous scenes is a stunt performer.

clue.text: Prepare to be shot again? Relax

definitions.meaning: to pose once more for a photograph

explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a firing squad but means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest or lie at ease is to relax; the second sense splits the word as re-pose.

clue.text: Smother with praise meal cooked without fault

indicators.note: the word for praise smothers, wraps around, the shuffled meal

parts.note: to bless is to praise

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of meal are reworked

explanation.surface: Lavish praise on a faultless meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges meal to AMEL, and 'Smother with' wraps the word for praise around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of fault or guilt means nobody can be held responsible.

clue.text: Resort very fashionable, not cold

parts.note: so means very

indicators.note: not means the letter for cold is left out

parts.note: chic means fashionable
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A trendy resort that isn't cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not cold' removes one C from CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A Black Sea city in Russia that is a holiday resort and hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics.

clue.text: Young bird's heading into tree

indicators.note: the letter goes into the tree's name

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree

indicators.note: the heading of bird is its first letter

explanation.surface: A young bird flies headlong into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' picks B from bird, which goes 'into' BAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Used before a noun, the word means small and young, as in baby carrots.

clue.text: Announced 6, big game

indicators.note: spoken out, so a word sounding like it is entered

parts.note: the answer to 6 down means the most recent news

explanation.surface: A notice announcing a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 down's answer means news; said 'Announced' it gives a homophone. 'Big game' is not a match but large hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest are large African antelopes hunted on safari, which makes them big game.

clue.text: Fast? Old and slow

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A paradox: something both fast and slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is the noun for abstinence, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking from Italian, telling players to perform slowly.

clue.text: Part of bridge nearly collapsed on Moriarty, for one

parts.note: an arch is part of a bridge

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fell means collapsed

explanation.surface: A bridge nearly fell on Sherlock Holmes's arch-enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims FELL to FEL. Professor Moriarty, Holmes's nemesis, is called 'the Napoleon of crime'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moriarty is the supreme criminal in the Sherlock Holmes stories, a master villain.

clue.text: One old king's returning in state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: coming back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's ancient king; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch returns to his own country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses LEARS to SRAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern country, a sovereign nation, is a state.

clue.text: Regularly delaying a relative's treatment

indicators.note: the letter a is put later in the word for regularly

parts.note: daily means regularly, every day
sis is a sister, a relative; the 's is is

explanation.surface: Regular delays to a relative's hospital treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying a' moves the A of DAILY later, giving DIALY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidney patients undergo this medical procedure, filtering the blood by machine, often several times a week.
